name: Reasoning Models Better Express Their Confidence
authors: Dongkeun Yoon, Seungone Kim, Sohee Yang, Sunkyoung Kim, Soyeon Kim, Yongil Kim, Eunbi Choi, Yireun Kim, Minjoon Seo et al. (KAIST; lead/first author Dongkeun Yoon, KAIST, work done during internship at LG AI Research; co-affiliations LG AI Research, CMU, UCL)
venue: NeurIPS 2025 (accepted); originally arXiv preprint (arXiv:2505.14489, v1 May 2025, v2 Oct 2025)
reflection_type: calibration/probing (verbalized confidence estimation analysis); the studied behavior is verbal self-critique via slow-thinking CoT (exploring alternatives, verifying, backtracking) used to adjust expressed confidence. The paper itself is an analysis/benchmarking study, not a new method.
feedback_source: self-generated (the model's own slow-thinking CoT dynamically adjusts verbalized confidence; no external tool/verifier/oracle is used to drive the confidence adjustment). For evaluation only, answer-correctness labels are matched against ground truth via GPT-4o mini to compute calibration metrics.
iteration_structure: single-shot (one CoT pass per question producing answer + verbalized confidence); analysis tracks confidence trajectory token-by-token within that single CoT. A discussion experiment (budget forcing, appending 'Wait,') tests extra inference rounds but does not reliably improve calibration.
reflection_object: output content (the verbalized/expressed confidence estimate) and the reasoning chain itself: the model reflects on its own chain-of-thought (via slow-thinking behaviors such as exploring alternatives, verifying, backtracking, epistemic markers) to dynamically refine the confidence it attaches to its answer. No prompt, skill, rules, code, or weights are modified.
requires_training: none (this is an inference-time analysis of existing reasoning vs non-reasoning models; the calibration gains require no weight update. Section 4.3 shows non-reasoning models gain calibration purely via in-context learning / few-shot slow-thinking exemplars). The reasoning models themselves were produced by prior RL/distillation, but no training is performed in this paper.
reward_or_critic_model: none (no reward model or external critic; confidence is self-expressed by the model through slow thinking. GPT-4o mini is used only as an answer-matching judge for scoring correctness, and GPT-4.1 is used only to edit CoTs in ablations — neither provides a learning/improvement signal).
distillation_target: none (reflection is not distilled into a persistent artifact in this paper). The closest related effect: in Section 4.3, R1-Distill-Qwen-32B slow-thinking traces are reused as few-shot in-context exemplars (prompt-level transfer) to elicit slow thinking in non-reasoning models, but this is in-context only, not a stored/optimized artifact.
emergent_vs_engineered: Primarily RL/distillation-emergent: the slow-thinking behaviors (exploring alternatives, backtracking, epistemic markers) that drive calibration emerge from how reasoning models (o1/R1-style) were trained, not from a hand-built reflection scaffold. The paper isolates this by showing Qwen3 (single checkpoint) is far better calibrated in Thinking vs Non-thinking mode, and that the behavior can also be elicited in non-reasoning models via engineered in-context demonstrations — i.e., the calibration gain is attributable to the slow-thinking process itself rather than to a specific training recipe.
memory_type: none (no persistent memory; analysis operates within a single CoT / scratchpad per question). For the in-context-learning experiment, a short-term in-context exemplar set (3 slow-thinking demonstrations) is used as prompt context, but nothing is stored across episodes.
memory_persistence: within-episode (confidence is adjusted only within a single chain-of-thought; no cross-episode/cross-task experience persistence).
memory_curation_mechanism: n/a (no memory store is maintained or curated).
error_localization_granularity: response-level for the headline calibration result (one confidence estimate per answer). The mechanistic analysis is finer-grained: token-level / step-level, since confidence is read out at each token position by appending '</think>\nAnswer:' to terminate reasoning early, revealing how confidence is refined across CoT steps (verification raises it, considering an alternative lowers it, rejecting the alternative raises it again).
intra_task_vs_inter_task: intra-task: confidence is refined within a single question's reasoning process; there is no transfer of experience across tasks/episodes. (The in-context exemplars in 4.3 are static demonstrations, not accumulated cross-task experience.)
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: mid-trajectory-recovery (in-flight): the model dynamically corrects/refines its expressed confidence during the CoT as it explores and rejects alternatives, rather than retrying after a failed episode or revising post-hoc.
task_domains: QA/reasoning (knowledge-focused factual QA and reasoning-intensive multiple-choice). Two task types: knowledge-focused (open-ended factual recall) and reasoning-intensive (math and non-math multiple-choice). Framed as foundational for trustworthy/reliable LLMs and uncertainty-aware LLM agents.
benchmarks: Six datasets/subsets: TriviaQA and NonambigQA (knowledge-focused; NonambigQA derived from AmbigQA/Natural Questions), plus Math and Non-Math subsets of MMLU-Pro and of SuperGPQA (reasoning-intensive multiple-choice). 1,000 examples uniformly sampled per dataset/subset; bootstrapping over resampled subsets for robustness.
headline_result: Six reasoning models (from four 32B-scale backbones) achieve strictly better verbalized confidence calibration than their non-reasoning counterparts in 33 out of 36 settings (6 model pairs x 6 datasets), measured by ECE (lower better), Brier Score (lower better), and AUROC (higher better). Gains hold even on knowledge-focused datasets where task accuracy is comparable, showing calibration gains are not merely a byproduct of better task accuracy.
baselines: Non-reasoning, instruction-tuned counterparts of each reasoning model: Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct (vs R1-Distill-Qwen-32B, QwQ-32B, Skywork-OR1-Preview-32B), GLM-4-32B-0414 (vs GLM-Z1-32B-0414), EXAONE-3.5-32B-Instruct (vs EXAONE-Deep-32B), and Qwen3-32B Non-thinking mode (vs Qwen3-32B Thinking mode). Also compared against advanced verbalized-confidence prompting baselines for non-reasoning models (Top-K, Multi-step) and an internal No-CoT lower bound.
gains_vs_baseline: Large ECE reductions on knowledge-focused data. Example (TriviaQA, Qwen2.5-32B group): Qwen2.5-Instruct ECE 0.129 vs R1-Distill-Qwen 0.042 and QwQ 0.063; AUROC 0.769 vs 0.807 (QwQ). Qwen3-32B: Non-thinking ECE 0.207 / AUROC 0.650 vs Thinking ECE 0.063 / AUROC 0.807 on TriviaQA (and on NonambigQA ECE 0.403 / AUROC 0.572 vs 0.226 / 0.757) for the same checkpoint. In-context slow-thinking (Table 5) improves non-reasoning models too: e.g., GLM-4-32B on TriviaQA ECE 0.150->0.029, AUROC 0.631->0.796; on NonambigQA ECE 0.338->0.126, AUROC 0.573->0.715. Calibration gap also widens with model size.
compute_cost_profile: Inference-time only; reasoning models incur the extra token cost of extended CoT (slow thinking) vs single-pass non-reasoning generation. Some reasoning models (R1-Distill, OR1-Preview, GLM-Z1) require a forced second inference round to elicit explicit Confidence Reasoning (regenerate up to </think> then re-prompt). Budget forcing (appending 'Wait,' for extra rounds) was tested but did not reliably improve calibration, indicating quality not quantity of slow thinking matters. No training compute (no gradient updates).
known_limitations: Reasoning models still tend toward high confidence, rarely assigning values below ~55%; lower task accuracy (e.g., NonambigQA) yields notably higher ECE/Brier, so residual overconfidence remains. Main experiments are limited to 32B-scale open models; proprietary o1/R1 not directly benchmarked. Calibration is for verbalized confidence specifically. The forced-Confidence-Reasoning procedure for some models, GPT-based answer matching and GPT-4.1-based CoT editing in ablations, and 1,000-example subsampling are potential sources of noise (mitigated via bootstrapping and manual inspection of 100 examples per ablation setting).
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: intrinsic-only for the confidence-adjustment mechanism: the model improves its expressed confidence purely through its own slow-thinking CoT with no external verifier, tool, or oracle label feeding into the confidence. Ground-truth labels are used only for offline evaluation/scoring of calibration, not as a correction signal.
self_correction_efficacy: net-positive: reasoning models become progressively better calibrated as the CoT unfolds (statistically significant improving slopes, p<0.05), while non-reasoning models show no such trend (sometimes worsening). This is a calibration (confidence) self-correction result rather than answer self-correction, and it improves without label leakage; removing slow-thinking (linearizing the CoT) significantly degrades calibration.
calibration_effect: improves: extended CoT / slow thinking strictly improves verbalized confidence calibration in 33/36 settings, directly contrasting the 'reasoning tax' / overconfidence concern. Ablations show non-linear reasoning (exploring alternatives, backtracking, refining) is the largest contributor; removing it degrades all three metrics, and removing epistemic markers causes overconfidence (worse ECE) though it can raise AUROC by collapsing predictions into two bins.
failure_attribution_capability: n/a (this work analyzes confidence calibration, not multi-agent failure attribution or a failure-mode taxonomy).
failure_mode_addressed: Targets/exposes LLM overconfidence and miscalibration ('sounding confident even when wrong') in verbalized confidence. Shows that slow thinking mitigates overconfidence and that linearized/fast reasoning (removing exploration, backtracking, and epistemic uncertainty markers) produces overconfident, less-calibrated outputs. Relevant to reasoning-model failure modes like superficial self-reflection and overconfidence rather than MAST multi-agent modes.
dataset_or_benchmark_released: No new benchmark dataset released; evaluation reuses TriviaQA, NonambigQA, MMLU-Pro, and SuperGPQA. Code (and prompts/evaluation pipeline) released at https://github.com/MattYoon/reasoning-models-confidence.
builds_on: Verbalized confidence estimation (Tian et al. 2023 'Just Ask for Calibration'; Xiong et al. 2024 'Can LLMs Express Their Uncertainty'; Geng et al. 2024 survey); calibration metrics ECE (Naeini et al. 2015 / Guo et al. 2017), Brier Score, AUROC; reasoning models / inference-time scaling (OpenAI o1 (Jaech et al. 2024), DeepSeek-R1, QwQ-32B, Skywork-OR1, GLM-Z1, EXAONE-Deep, Qwen3); slow-thinking / cognitive-behavior characterization (Gandhi et al. 2025; Min et al. 2024 'imitate'); 'know what they know' calibration (Kadavath et al. 2022); budget forcing (Muennighoff et al. 2025, s1); in-context learning (Dong et al. 2022 survey).
extended_by_or_inspired: Cited by follow-up work on reasoning-model confidence/uncertainty, e.g. 'Thinking Out Loud: Do Reasoning Models Know When They're Right?' (Zeng, Xuan et al.) and 'Verbalized Confidence Triggers Self-...' (verbalized-confidence self-correction work) indexed on Semantic Scholar; broadly part of the 2025 line analyzing calibration of o1/R1-style reasoning models (concurrent work zhang2025reasoning trains a hidden-state probe over CoT, contrasted in the paper).
reasoning_model_native: Yes — the paper specifically targets and holds for o1/R1-style reasoning models with extended-CoT slow thinking; its central thesis is that the built-in slow-thinking/reflective behavior of these models is what produces better verbalized confidence calibration, and that eliciting the same behavior (Qwen3 Thinking mode, or in-context slow-thinking in non-reasoning models) reproduces the benefit.
on_policy_distillation_link: Indirect/weak: the studied reasoning models include distilled ones (R1-Distill-Qwen, derived from DeepSeek-R1 distillation), and Section 4.3 reuses R1-Distill-Qwen-32B's own slow-thinking traces as in-context exemplars (an on-policy-style transfer of reflective behavior into other models), but the paper does no on-policy distillation or skill-optimization itself; this is an analysis of inference-time behavior.
sample_efficiency: n/a — no training/iterative trials to reach the result; it is a single-pass inference benchmark. Calibration improves monotonically along a single CoT (the longer/slow-thinking the CoT, the better-calibrated), but forcing additional inference rounds (budget forcing) does not reliably improve calibration further.
